extracted.intended_audience: NIH F99/K00 fellowship applicants and reviewers; grant applicants preparing human subjects, inclusion, recruitment, and institutional training sections
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and documentation of an NIH F99/K00 fellowship application sections including institutional environment/training plan, human subjects protections, inclusion of women/minorities/children, recruitment/retention, and study procedures/timeline. Focuses on compliance and demonstrating feasibility/support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are Human Subjects Involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement whether human subjects are involved (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must declare involvement; affects whether follow-up human subjects protections, IRB review, and clinical trial questions apply. (Page shows checkbox: Yes selected.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the Project Exempt from Federal regulations / Exemption Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if the study is exempt from federal human subjects regulations and provide applicable exemption number(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming exemption, supply the exemption number. If not exempt, provide the relevant protections and IRB submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Questionnaire (Clinical trial determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer whether participants are prospectively assigned to an intervention, whether the study evaluates the effect of an intervention, and whether the effect is a health-related biomedical or behavioral outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all subitems (1.4.a–1.4.d). Provide a ClinicalTrials.gov identifier if applicable. These answers determine whether the project is a Clinical Trial for NIH policy and influence required reporting/registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Title and Basic Information (clear, specific title)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a specific study title describing the focus and context of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a title that clearly communicates study aims and context (example: 'Examining the Longitudinal Influence of the Physical and Social Environments on Social Isolation and Cognitive Health: contextualizing the role of technology').

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Population Characteristics (conditions or focus of study)
rubrics_metrics.description: List the conditions or focal constructs (e.g., social isolation, cognitive functioning) and describe population sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify datasets or parent trials (e.g., NHATS, I-CONECT) and describe relevant cohort characteristics and recruitment sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Criteria (inclusion/exclusion criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify explicit eligibility criteria and the source population (e.g., participants of NHATS or I-CONECT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define how participants are sampled (purposeful sampling for qualitative focus groups), group assignment restrictions (only participants who have completed parent trial to avoid contamination), and any demographic or clinical inclusion/exclusion rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: State minimum and maximum age limits for study participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit min/max ages (example: Min Age: 65 Years; Max Age: N/A). If no max, state as such and justify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe representation of women, racial/ethnic minorities, and whether children are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide demographics of existing datasets (e.g., NHATS baseline percentages), state purposeful sampling to increase diversity, and explicitly state that no children will participate if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and Retention Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe recruitment sources and procedures, outreach methods, scheduling and confirmation, and retention strategies (or rationale if inapplicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example procedures: contact eligible individuals by phone, explain study purpose/rights, schedule sessions, confirm attendance 5 days prior. For non-longitudinal qualitative work, retention plan may be inapplicable and should be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Existing Dataset / Resource
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the study uses existing datasets/resources and provide details (domestic/foreign, enrollment locations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using existing datasets (Yes), report the dataset name(s) and enrollment country(ies) (example: NHATS, USA). Include planned vs actual enrollment reporting when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment Targets and Inclusion Enrollment Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide planned enrollment numbers, demographic breakdowns (race/ethnicity/sex), and IER reporting details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply tables or counts for racial and ethnic categories, cumulative actuals vs planned, and ensure consistency with NIH inclusion reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Timeline and Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a study timeline with activities mapped to years (IRB submission, secondary analyses, focus groups, manuscript prep, conference presentations, progression to F99/K00 phases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include anticipated enrollment of first subject and year-by-year milestones for F99 and K00 phases; show feasibility by aligning tasks with award periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects — Involvement, Characteristics, and Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how human subjects are involved, sample sizes, sites, design elements (secondary analysis, primary qualitative data collection), and sampling rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State cohort sizes (e.g., NHATS N=8,334; I-CONECT target 320), number of focus groups and target participants per group, multi-site arrangements, and justification of purposive sampling for diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Procedures and Materials (detailed methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed procedures for secondary and primary data collection/analysis, intervention description, assessment schedule, and recording protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe intervention dose/frequency (e.g., video-chat 30 min/day, 4x/week for 6 months, then 2x/week maintenance), baseline/6/12 month assessments, in-home visits, MRIs if safe, audio/video recording for speech analysis, and equipment (e.g., electronic pillboxes at one site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Risks (risk characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify potential risks to participants (e.g., mild discomfort discussing social isolation, confidentiality risks) and estimate risk level (minimal or greater).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why risk is minimal, describe de-identification, separate storage of contact information, and participant rights to decline answering or withdraw; include compensation policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed Consent and Assent (process and documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe consent procedures, who obtains consent, timing, consent documentation, and special provisions (e.g., participants with MCI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain additional informed consent for focus groups even if parent study consent exists; present written consent before data collection; participants with MCI may provide consent; store consent forms in locked cabinets for specified retention period (example: three years unless IRB waives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection Against Risk / Confidentiality Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe measures to protect confidentiality and data security (de-identification, storage, access controls, destruction plans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: clean and recode secondary data prior to PI access; store primary transcripts and notes in password-protected files; keep contact info separate from data; limit access to research team and HSPP; destroy original focus group summaries after an appropriate time; publish/present results only in anonymous/aggregated form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan (DSMP) and Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether a DSMB will be appointed and describe the data and safety monitoring approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate Yes/No for DSMB appointment (example: No selected). If multi-site or higher-risk interventions, articulate monitoring frequency and responsibilities or single-IRB arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-site Study and Single IRB Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: If multi-site, indicate use of same protocol across sites and describe single IRB plan or designate N/A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-site studies using the same protocol, provide a single IRB plan describing oversight and coordination across sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Structure of the Study Team (roles and coordination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the study team structure, roles (PI, research assistant), and coordination with parent study teams for recruitment and logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define who conducts recruitment calls, who leads focus groups, who records/notes sessions, and how partner sites (e.g., I-CONECT teams at OHSU/UM) assist with recruitment and space booking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Parent Study Data and Resources (feasibility/support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document access to existing data (e.g., I-CONECT R01 projects), institutional cores, and resources that support the proposed training and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters from co-sponsors should state access to data, plans for involving the trainee in data analysis/manuscript preparation, and use of institutional cores (recruitment, neuroimaging, data management) to demonstrate feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation and Participant Logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide plans for arranging participant transportation to study sessions when needed to facilitate participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe arrangements for transport to/from focus groups to remove participation barriers and protect participant privacy during sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB Training and Research Personnel Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all research personnel who contact participants, take notes, transcribe recordings, or assist with analysis have IRB training and are added to IRB records before activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document training status and inclusion on IRB applications; restricted access to identifiable data only to trained personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant Rights and Compensation Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe participants' rights to not answer questions, withdraw at any time, and compensation policies even if participants do not complete activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly in consent forms that withdrawal has no penalty and compensation will be provided for time/effort even if activities are not completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Retention and Destruction Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify how long informed consents and primary data are stored and describe destruction procedures for original summaries/transcripts after appropriate retention period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: store signed consent in locked cabinet for three years after completion unless IRB requires otherwise, and destroy original focus group summaries at appropriate time after analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Structure and Institutional Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional PhD program structure, required coursework and milestones, teaching requirements, and additional program resources that support trainee development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required course units beyond master's (e.g., minimum 45 units), year-by-year curricular expectations, qualifying exam requirements (written paper of publishable quality plus oral defense), teaching obligations in years 3–4, and availability of research clusters, seminars, office space, labs, and graduate school resources (grant writing, professional development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and Evaluation of Trainee Progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe formal monitoring procedures (end-of-semester reports, yearly progress timelines) used to track milestones and deliverables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require End of Semester Reports completed by faculty mentor including milestones (proposals, publications, presentations) and an annual Progress Report Timeline co-signed by student and mentor, submitted to program director and graduate school.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship Track Record and Sponsor Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Document mentors' past success mentoring trainees, history of mentees receiving NIH career awards, and explicit commitments to mentor the applicant through both award phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should state mentors' experience (e.g., >25 years dementia research, mentorship of >10 postdocs with NIH K/R funding), their plan to involve trainee in ongoing R01 projects, use of cores, and provide continuous mentorship across pre-doctoral and postdoctoral stages.
